build: Remember (REM) crack with trainers and highscore saver, one load; the engine is unpacked before the cracker's menu

exclude: the cracker's documents and the code that pages through them
RAM under the KERNAL: the cracker's trainer and highscore-saver menu

comments.text: Cracker's code: restores the system interrupt, loads the highscore file H.PATROL HI from drive 8 through the KERNAL and runs on.
Reads CIA1 port B and returns the stick state; bit 4 is fire, bits 0-3 up, down, left, right, all clear when pressed.
Runs when the plane has been hit (collision flags $3D): finds the record that hit, and if its state allows it starts the plane's crash ($3F = 1).
Sets the video bank (CIA2 port A low bits to %10), clears zero page $02-$52, copies the sprite register table at $8030 to the video chip and shows the score line ($2EE0).

Draws the title screen: character set $02, draws the highscore table ($0F90, $1210), then waits for fire (CIA1 port B bit 4 on $DC01) while the name-entry routine at $12D0 runs when a new score has made the table.
Compares the five score digits at $13-$17 with the five highscore rows on screen at $4122 + n*$50 and, when the score beats one, shifts the lower rows down and writes the score into its row ($1256).
Highscore name entry: stick left and right move a cursor over the alphabet row, fire accepts a letter, up to twelve letters, then continues at $0C55.
Points the IRQ vector $0314 at $13AB, enables the video chip's raster and sprite-sprite collision interrupts, sets the first raster line to $D2, and clears the collision latches.

Raster interrupt handler. Three bands per frame (index in $20): the sky band loads the first sprite register table from $8060, the next band the second from $8090, the last band sets the status panel (background colour $0B, 40-column text) and returns the index to 0. Sprite-sprite collisions are latched into $3D, $3E.
Entry the cracker's menu jumps to after a highscore choice: sets up the sound chip's voice 3 as a noise source ($1900), the video chip and ports ($1170), then falls into the per-life loop at $1456.
Start of each life: restarts the music, draws the playfield and the shoreline ($11A0), copies the status line ($14D0), then runs the frame loop below until the lives counter ($40) goes negative.

One pass of the game's main loop, run once per frame in practice: read the stick ($1920), steer ($193C), scroll the ground ($1670), spawn and move each family of objects, resolve hits ($2400), play sound ($25A0), advance the enemy planes ($2700). The pass ends when $40 is negative.
Called every 8th frame by $1720. Depending on the scroll speed $22 it scrolls the ground rows one column left or right ($15C0, $1600), so the landscape appears to move sideways.
Scrolls the ground rows of the screen one character left, bounded by the row pointers set in $1550.
Scrolls the ground rows of the screen one character right, bounded by the row pointers set in $1550.
Sets the pointer $2E/$2F to the 16-byte object record number $30 in the table at $80C0 (the player's shots); the other family pointers are $19D0, $1E00, $2130 and $2640.
Spawns a shot when the fire test passed (the front record is free) and advances every record of the shot table; a shot hits the ground rows through the table at $8400.
Moves the four records of the first object table sideways by the scroll speed and, for those that are due this frame, down the screen; calls the ground scroll every 8th frame.
Clears a record of the first table once its screen position reaches $58 or more.

Sorts the records of the first table by their vertical position and writes their sprite positions, enable bits and colours into the sprite register tables at $8060 and $8090, so three sprites can show in each band.
Sets CIA1 timer A running, starts voice 3 of the sound chip as a noise generator (frequency high byte $80) and clears bit 0 of the processor port at $01.
Reads the voice 3 oscillator ($D41B) into $33 as a random number, CIA1 timer A into $34/$35 and the raster line into $36 for the same purpose, then reads the stick through $0D14 into $1F.
Every 8th frame turns the stick into scroll speed $22 (right: up to +2, left: down to -2) and climb rate $37 (down: +1, up: -1); fire ($1F bit 4 clear) starts a shot through $1E40.
Puts the plane's shadow and sprite on screen: sets the sprite pointers from the scroll speed and moves the plane's vertical position ($8061) by $37, between $52 and $A0.
Sets $2E/$2F to the 16-byte record number $30 in the table at $8530, a second family of objects.
Spawns a record of the second family when the random byte $33 is zero, then moves every record of the family by its own speed and by the template record at $8570; ends by calling $1AD9 and $1BD0.
Goes through the second family's four records: tests each for a collision through $2220, applies its state bits to its movement, and counts the records that moved in $39.
Sorts the records of the second family by their vertical position and writes their sprite positions and colours.
Takes the first free record of the shots at $8670 and starts a shot at the plane's position with speed $A0.
Moves each shot of the table at $8670 and tests them against the ground rows.
Sorts the third family of records by vertical position and writes their sprites.
Moves the record at $2E/$2F sideways by the scroll speed $22 (or by its own speed byte), with the carry into the record's high x bit.
Chooses the shadow sprite pointer from the plane's height ($8061) and the scroll direction.
Uses the collision flags $3D and $3E to find which records were hit: marks them destroyed ($40 in byte 15), adds 50 or 100 to the score ($2540), and plays the explosion sound ($23F5).

While $3F is not zero the plane is exploding: the first pass copies a block of sound settings from $8B00 to the sound chip, then every second frame the plane's sprite pointer takes the next picture ($3F high nibble + $9E), and at $A0 steps a life is taken ($40) and the level state is cleared ($2480).
Clears the object tables at $8530-$856F and $8670-$868F, the plane's state, and puts the plane back at height $A0; waits for a moment and restarts the sound.
Clears the score and the playfield pointers, sets four lives ($40), copies the highscore rows and the stage state and starts the first stage.
Adds the value in A to the score digits at $13-$17 (carry between digits) and writes the five digits to the status line at $4771.
Sets the engine tone on voice 1 from the table at $8850 and starts it.
Sets the pitch of voice 1 from the plane's height ($8061) so the engine note changes as the plane climbs or dives; then runs the explosion sound routine twice.
Starts an enemy plane in a free record of the table at $8880: its fields come from the voice 3 random number, the raster line and CIA1 timer A.

Spawns and moves the enemy planes of the table at $8880: when a plane's x reaches the matching record of the template table at $88A0 it takes that record's fields; planes that pass their end point are replaced; calls $2780 and $2820 to place them in sprites.

Every 32 frames starts a record of the table at $87A0 (twelve records of three bytes), then moves every active record by the scroll speed and writes a pattern for it into the ground picture around $4907.

Picks one of four texts from the pointers at $8B90 by comparing $45 with $10, $30 and $40, copies it to $479C and the colour to $DB9C, and copies the line at $8B40 to $44A4; the plane is put back at height $A0.
Copies the five score digits and the stage number to the status line at $4023 and $401B.
Calls $22D0 when the stage flag $41 is clear, and $2CD0 once the target run has begun.
Entry of Rob Hubbard's music driver: JMP to its first routine; $A003 is the second entry.
The driver's per-frame player.
